name: claude-quenching
description: OKF-centric knowledge-base aligner for the Claude Code surface of any repository. It acts on three fronts — the docs/ OKF bundle, the native specs/ spec-driven workspace, and the .claude/ skill + command surface — behind one symmetric interface: every front has an align (structure, one pass) and an align-and-update (structure plus content, looped to a fixpoint), and /align and /align-and-update run all three in dependency order on a single confirmation. Around them: inserts knowledge into the right home, curates a fixed A–Z glossary, drains project memory into docs, refactors CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md into thin pointers, imports external sources as OKF docs, builds and maintains the mkdocs site over the documentation/ home, parks and triages a task backlog, mints skills, and drives the plan cycle (status → explore → propose → apply → archive, or abandon; plus from-claude, which turns a Claude Code plan into an archivable one) with the bundle as its knowledge substrate — entirely native, no external CLI, no delta, no separate spec store: a plan writes durable rules straight into docs/standards/, isolated on a branch, and two deterministic Python tools (okf-validate.py, specs.py) give the skills their rails. Twenty-seven skills, all under one quenching-<front>-<object>-<verb> taxonomy, each user-invocable: false behind a thin command wrapper (/docs:*, /specs:*, /skill:*, and the root /align, /align-and-update). Every repository that adopts it looks the same.
